title: 清平乐（春归何处）
titleEn: Pure Serene Music (Where Has Spring Gone?)
author: 黄庭坚
intro: The poet treats spring like a friend who has wandered off: where did it go? If anyone knows, call it back! Maybe the oriole knows — but nobody understands its song, and it flies away.
analysis: 这首词写“惜春”（舍不得春天离开）。作者把春天当成一个人来写：春天回到哪里去了？到处冷冷清清，找不到它走过的路。如果有人知道春天去了哪儿，请把它叫回来，和我住在一起。下阕更有意思：春天没留下脚印，谁知道它在哪儿呢？大概只能问黄鹂鸟了。可是黄鹂叫了又叫，没有人听得懂；它借着风，飞过蔷薇花丛，也走了。蔷薇是初夏开的花，看到蔷薇，就知道春天真的走了。全词用问答的形式，一问再问，越找越找不到，语言像说话一样自然，却写出了一种天真又落寞的心情。
analysisEn: This lyric is about “cherishing spring” — not wanting it to leave. Huang Tingjian writes about spring as if it were a person who has wandered off. Where has spring gone? Everything is quiet and lonely, and there is no path to follow. If anyone knows where it went, please call it back to live with me. The second half is playful. Spring left no footprints, so who could know? Perhaps only the oriole. But the bird sings and sings, and no one can understand it; then it rides the wind over the roses and away. Roses bloom in early summer, so the moment we see them we know spring really has gone. The whole poem is a chain of questions, each answer leading to another dead end, written in language as natural as speech. Under the childlike game of hide-and-seek lies a quiet loneliness — the feeling of reaching for something beautiful just after it has slipped away.
background: Huang Tingjian (1045–1105) was one of the most famous poets and calligraphers of the Northern Song and a close friend and follower of Su Shi. He suffered repeated exile for political reasons; some scholars date this lyric to his final exile in Yizhou, in today’s Guangxi.
pronunciation: 词牌“清平乐”的“乐”读 yuè。“谁知”的“谁”按诗词传统读 shuí（统编教材在诗词中多注 shuí，今天口语一般读 shéi）。“去处”的“处”读 chù。“唤取”“问取”的“取”是助词，仍读 qǔ。啭 zhuàn。
version: 采用通行文本（《山谷词》）。“因风飞过蔷薇”有的本子作“因风吹过蔷薇”，网站不用。

lines.en: Where has spring gone home to?
All is quiet, and it left no trail.

lines.py: ruò yǒu rén zhī chūn qù chù
lines.lit: If there is someone who knows where spring went,
lines.en: If anyone knows where spring has gone,

lines.py: huàn qǔ guī lái tóng zhù
lines.lit: call it to come back and live together.
lines.en: call it back to stay here with me.

lines.py: chūn wú zōng jì shuí zhī
lines.lit: Spring has no traces — who knows?
lines.en: Spring left no footprints — who could know?

lines.py: chú fēi wèn qǔ huáng lí
lines.en: No one, unless we ask the oriole.

lines.py: bǎi zhuàn wú rén néng jiě
lines.lit: A hundred trills, no one can understand;
lines.en: It sings and sings, but no one understands,

lines.py: yīn fēng fēi guò qiáng wēi
lines.lit: on the wind it flies past the roses.
lines.en: and on the wind it flies off over the roses.

words.note: 取：动词后的助词，没有实际意义。
一种黄色的鸣禽，春天叫声最多。
现代汉语“理解”“了解”的“解”。
初夏开花，现代汉语仍用。

imagery.name: 春
imagery.zh: 春天被写成一个会走路、会离开的人，作者想把它找回来。
imagery.en: Spring is a person who can walk away, and the poet wants to bring it back.

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: 黄鹂好像知道春天去了哪里，可它的话没人听得懂，最后也飞走了。
imagery.en: The oriole seems to know where spring went, but nobody understands its song — and then it leaves too.

imagery.name: 蔷薇
imagery.zh: 蔷薇在初夏开放，黄鹂飞过蔷薇，暗示春天已经彻底过去。
imagery.en: Roses bloom in early summer, so the bird flying over them quietly tells us spring is truly over.
